# `connectome`

the fiber counts between the regions of a partition of the end surface (a measurement over the partition), from a fiber bundle's ends.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run connectome --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run connectome --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run connectome --fibers tracts --end-surface pial --over desikan-killiany [--smooth-hops N] [--max-end-distance MM|none] --dataset d --subject s
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `fibers` | manifold curve, where {"name": "$fibers"} | yes |
| `surface` | manifold surface, where {"name": "$end_surface"} | yes |
| `partition` | selection set, manifold surface.manifold.0, where {"name": "$over"} | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fibers` | `--fibers` | `required` | - |  | the fiber bundle's name (the subject's own: `curve/<name>`) |
| `end_surface` | `--end-surface` | `required` | - |  | the surface the fibers' ends are placed on (a location on the cortex, not a depth) |
| `over` | `--over` | `required` | - |  | the partition of the end surface the counts are reduced over: a parcellation or a tile level of the ladder |
| `smooth_hops` | `--smooth-hops` | `0` | hops |  | hops of the mesh smoothing, applied to the partition's memberships (0: the plain fiber count) |
| `max_end_distance` | `--max-end-distance` | `5` | mm |  | a fiber with an end farther than this from the end surface is left out; none: no gate (the reference) |
| `points_per_fiber` | `--points-per-fiber` | `0` | points |  | the points of each fiber (read from the bundle when 0) |
| `name` | `--name` | `{fibers}_{end_surface}_fiber_counts` | - |  | the stored name of the counts |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`meeg.fiber_ends`](../nodes.md) | fibers=fibers | points_per_fiber=$points_per_fiber | end_points |
| before | [`meeg.nearest_vertex`](../nodes.md) | points=end_points, positions=surface |  | end_vertex, end_distance |
| before | [`meeg.end_gate`](../nodes.md) | end_distance=end_distance | max_end_distance_mm=$max_end_distance | keep |
| before | [`meeg.smooth_memberships`](../nodes.md) | label=partition, faces=surface | hops=$smooth_hops | memberships |
| before | [`meeg.partition_counts`](../nodes.md) | end_vertex=end_vertex, keep=keep, memberships=memberships |  | counts |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `counts` | kind measurement, name $name, over partition, of fibers, codes 2, unit fibers, description fiber_count (connection_weight when smoothed) between the regions of the partition, both orders, the within-region count at the diagonal |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE STRUCTURAL CONNECTOME OVER A PARTITION (spec docs/specs/2026-11-16-structural-connectome.md; outputs: docs/specs/2026-11-17-definition-outputs.md).

  nxr-neuro run connectome --fibers tracts --end-surface pial --over desikan-killiany [--smooth-hops N] [--max-end-distance MM|none] --dataset d --subject s

`--fibers`, `--end-surface` and `--over` are REQUIRED (each is a choice of data): their default is `required`, which the reader refuses to run with.
The counts are a MEASUREMENT over the partition: the fibers are the elements, the region pairs the members; two codes a row (the region and the other), both orders, the
within-region pairs stored (a fiber with both ends in one region adds 2 at its diagonal). Smoothing is pushed onto the memberships (the adjoint of the mesh's smoothing step):
the vertex matrix is never formed here. Default smoothing: 0 hops for a partition (3 at the vertex level, `connectome_vertices`).
The fibers and the surface keep the precision they are stored in (no widening); a pair stored in different precision is refused, naming both.
```
